result.summary: Makes ArgsManager report a fatal startup error when a non-list configuration option is assigned multiple times in the same section of a configuration file. Options flagged with ALLOW_LIST remain repeatable.
result.problem: When a single-value option is assigned multiple times in the same config file section, Bitcoin Core silently discards one of the values according to counterintuitive precedence rules. Node operators may unknowingly run with discarded settings, and supporting this behavior requires complex reverse-precedence code in settings merging.
evidence: PR description: 'Instead of silently ignoring settings, this change makes it an error to provide an ambiguous config file that provides assigns multiple values to a single-value setting.'

PR description: 'Part of the motivation for this change is to improve usability and prevent settings that look valid from being silently ignored. Another motivation is to be able to remove confusing "reverse precedence" logic in #17581'
result.scope_notes: This PR sits on top of #16545 and #17580. Only the top two commits (c578547bcf5 and 08548ef76c0) are unique to this pull request; the rest belong to the underlying stack.
result.changed_since_previous: Rebased onto updated base PRs #16545 and #17580 with intermediate review fixes and documentation adjustments; the PR's own commits remain functionally identical.
result.card: Bitcoin Core currently ignores duplicate assignments of single-value options within the same section of a configuration file, which can silently discard intended settings under obscure precedence rules. This PR makes multiple assignments of non-list settings in the same config section a startup error, alerting operators to ambiguous configurations. It also unblocks #17581 to remove reverse-precedence logic in config merging. The PR is stacked on top of open PRs #16545 and #17580.

risk.why: Stricter configuration validation will cause nodes with existing duplicate config entries to fail on startup instead of booting.
